extracted.intended_audience: students of literature, aspiring novelists, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying E. M. Forster’s criteria for evaluating novels (fantasy, prophecy, pattern/rhythm, character, use of mythology, etc.) as presented in his lecture-style critical prose. Useful for close reading, literary criticism, and novel-writing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fantasy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fantasy: 'It implies the supernatural, but need not express it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The genre can include literal supernatural beings or situations but also subtler interventions; fantasy needn't always overtly present the supernatural to qualify. Accepts a range of implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devices of the fantastic
rubrics_metrics.description: List of devices used by writers of the fantastic: 'the introduction of a god, ghost, angel, monkey, monster, midget, witch into ordinary life; or the introduction of ordinary men into no man’s land, the future, the past, the interior of the earth, the fourth dimension; or divings into and dividings of personality; or finally the device of parody or adaptation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These devices are 'strictly limited' in number but can be reinvented; recognizing which device is used helps classify and understand a fantastic work. The limited set suggests the 'beam of light can only be manipulated in certain ways.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation and freshness of fantastic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Although devices are limited, 'they will occur naturally to writers of a certain temperament, and be put to fresh use.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluator should note whether a work merely repeats an old device or re-energizes it. Originality in fantasy often comes from fresh treatment rather than new devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merging magic and common sense (mark of the true fantasist)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'mark of the true fantasist' is to 'merge the kingdoms of magic and common sense by using words that apply to both, and the mixture he has created comes alive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful fantasy blends ordinary detail and fantastic element so both remain credible; watch for language that legitimately fits both realms (examples: the motor-bus that turns upside down yet returns as if nothing happened).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definiteness of character in fantasy
rubrics_metrics.description: A character may be 'slightly sketched' yet 'individual, and this definiteness causes the book to grip.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in fantasy, clear, individual characterization (even if economical) secures reader engagement. Lack of individual definition weakens grip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative method in fantasy: Socratic method, tension, shocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective fantasist technique: 'It proceeds with a growing tension, a series of little shocks. The method is Socratic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate pacing and structure: does the work build tension through iterative thought-experiments or choices (Socratic probing) producing escalating shocks? This method produces intellectual and emotional momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantasy theme recurrence (e.g., the wishing-ring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain motifs recur (example: 'the old old story of the wishing ring which brings either misery or nothing at all'); fantasies 'contain scarcely anything that is new.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how a new work varies, refines, or deepens familiar motifs rather than expecting wholly novel plots; surprises arise from fresh minds working with old notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody or adaptation as a creative device
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody/adaptation: the fantasist 'adopts for his mythology some earlier work and uses it as a framework or quarry for his own purposes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: gives writers a scaffold when they struggle to create original character worlds (examples: The Magic Flute, Ulysses). Pitfalls: may lead to a 'false start' where parody gives way to a separate serious work (Joseph Andrews). Evaluate fidelity, transformative use, and whether the borrowed mythology serves the new work's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mythology to create coherence in experimental works
rubrics_metrics.description: A guiding mythology can enable coherence in unusual or experimental structures (example: Joyce using the Odyssey to hold Ulysses together).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing an experimental novel, note whether an underlying mythology provides structural unity and thematic resonance across disparate episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecy as an aspect: tone of voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophecy (in Forster's sense) is 'a tone of voice' implying various faiths or exalted views; it's not foretelling but an accent that 'will filter into the turns of the novelist’s phrase.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a novel's voice aspires to universality or the numinous; prophetic tone affects diction, focus, and the novel's relation to common sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader qualities required for prophetic fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetic aspect 'demands two qualities: humility and the suspension of the sense of humour.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics/readers should approach prophetic works with humility (to hear the prophet) and suppress ironic laughter that reduces serious or exalted tone to a 'figure of fun.' Failure to adopt these stances may misread the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophet vs preacher distinction (Dostoevsky vs George Eliot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preacher (George Eliot) keeps God and tables 'in the same plane' and treats pity as localized; Prophet (Dostoevsky) lets characters and situations 'stand for more than themselves' so 'infinity attends them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating moral/exalted fiction, determine whether the writer localizes religious/moral feeling into scenes (preacher) or enlarges characters into universal symbols (prophet). This affects scope, diction, and the reader's sense of expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic implication in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: In prophetic writing 'every sentence he writes implies this extension' (characters expanding to universals); 'the implication is the dominant aspect of his work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for prose that constantly suggests larger metaphysical or moral dimensions beyond the immediate incident; measure how convincingly ordinary detail is made to signify universals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional externalization as a prophetic device (Wuthering Heights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotions in certain novels 'function differently': they 'surround' characters 'like thunder clouds' and 'generate the explosions' that fill the novel; emotions externalize into setting and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the novel externalizes inner states into atmosphere, landscape, and dramatic events, rather than confining emotion inside characters; such externalization can create powerful mythic or prophetic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern (shape) and rhythm in the novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern (borrowed term) springs mainly out of the plot; Forster gives pictorial images (a book 'the shape of an hour-glass' or 'the shape of a grand chain') to explain how pattern organizes a work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the novel's large-scale structure/pattern (convergences, symmetries, repetitions). Example: Thais as an hour-glass where two characters converge, cross and recede with 'mathematical precision'—such patterning contributes to reader pleasure and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm as a literary quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm (a vague but important term) arises from pattern and plot and is an aspect to which readers must attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically examine sentence, scene, and plot pacing to discern recurring beats or movements that constitute a work's rhythm; readers who cannot articulate 'rhythm' should still detect its effects on pleasure and coherence.
